content:
Alex M.: folks — switchboard (Fintech) just asked for a POC to replace their current vendor. they want: prompt parity, identical function-calling behavior, and answers to their security questionnaire. can we outline blockers and who owns what?
Priya S.: thanks Alex. sales ask: 3mo POC, ~200k monthly tokens baseline, ramp to 1M. they want pricing guidance + any delta risks on responses. also encryption at rest + SSO are musts.
Devon (Sales): pricing: propose hosted + committed discount for first 3 months, then evaluate Dedicated if tail latency or throughput becomes an issue. question: will we bill same token contract as vendor? they want predictable invoicing for procurement.
Luca (Eng): quick summary of technical gaps we typically see: tokenization differences (affects token counts), truncation/stop-token semantics, function-calling signature differences, and micro-variation in responses. for parity we do three things: 1) request/response mapping shim, 2) prompt normalization layer, 3) heuristic post-filtering to emulate vendor quirks.
Samir (SE): I can run side-by-side comparison. ask them for a representative sample of ~100 prompts (happy path + edge). we should produce a diff report with: token delta, response drift, function name mismatches, and latency percentiles.
Alex M.: they already sent 12 sample requests. attaching snippet they gave:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <old_api_key>
{
  "model":"g-v3-small",
  "input":"Summarize transaction history for 2025-02-01 to 2025-02-28",
  "return_functions": true
}
```
Luca (Eng): mapping notes: our function-calling uses `functions` array and `tool_call` token in responses. vendor uses `return_functions: true`. easiest approach: adapter translates vendor payload -> our SDK call, and rewrites response field names. edge-case: vendor sometimes returns function payload as JSON string with single quotes — we should robust-parse.
Priya S.: security questionnaire red flags from Switchboard: data residency (EU data must stay in eu-west-1), key management (customer KMS), and deletion certification. legal will want a template answer.
sec-bot: reminder: Redwood Private or Dedicated required for customer KMS + EU data residency constraint. SOC2 + ISO27001 docs are on the vault: https://redwood.internal/compliance.
Devon (Sales): procurement will push for pay-per-use. we should show both options: (A) hosted per-token with 15% POC discount, (B) 3mo committed reserved capacity with monthly invoice cap. include churn protection clause.
Samir (SE): practical parity approach: 1) run 100-case SxS test, 2) produce 3 candidate normalization rules (stop tokens, stop-on-sentence-boundary, function-name mapping), 3) choose one to A/B in POC. can automate with a small runner.
Alex M.: any infra blockers for POC? they want IP allowlist, short-lived certs for staging, and egress lock.
Luca (Eng): infra notes: we can provide allowlist of outbound IPs from Hosted (list will be provided), or spin a Dedicated env in eu-west-1 for full isolation. short-lived certs: use our provisioning API; will need their admin to accept CA fingerprint. network test will take ~2 days.
Priya S.: timeline proposal: kickoff M+1 week, SxS tests in week 2, security questionnaire answers + contract redlines by week 3, POC run week 4–8.
Devon (Sales): enterprise blocker: procurement demands vendor equivalency for function-calling determinism. they want a statement that we won't change function signatures mid-contract. can legal commit to that?
Samir (SE): we can commit to stable function-signature guarantees on the served model surface for the duration of the contract but add an escape clause for critical security patches. we should define "stable" in the SOW.
Luca (Eng): one more technical nuance: token-based billing differences — vendor counts subword tokens differently. propose we release a small token-compat shim that reports token counts normalized to vendor method for POC invoicing.
Alex M.: action items: @Samir collect their 100 prompts (they sent 12 so far), @Luca prepare mapping shim repo and quick runbook, @Priya draft pricing options + timeline, @sec-bot or sec team prepare Qs answers for data residency & KMS.
Priya S.: i'll draft pricing + SOW. leaning to offer Hosted+3mo commit with opt-in Dedicated migration.
Devon (Sales): flagging procurement: ask for a short 1-pager that maps vendor feature X -> Redwood feature Y (function-calling parity, streaming semantics, retry behavior).
Samir (SE): i'll start the runner today. need their API keys + sample responses. ping me in DM. :rocket: 
Luca (Eng): i'll spin a eu-west-1 Dedicated sandbox if procurement requires isolation — need an internal ticket, ETA 4 business days.
sec-bot: noted. security review will start once we have their questionnaire attached to the ticket.
Alex M.: great — i'll consolidate and send to Switchboard. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
